title: Avalanche: Optimizing Cache Utilization via Matrix Reordering for Sparse Matrix Multiplication Accelerator
problem: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) accelerators suffer from poor on-chip memory utilization due to irregular memory access patterns; existing designs fail to cache both input matrices efficiently, leading to redundant DRAM accesses and low throughput.
motivation: SpMM is ubiquitous in scientific computing and graph workloads, and as models grow sparser, on-chip memory utilization becomes the primary performance limiter rather than raw compute throughput.
method: Avalanche keeps both input matrices in a small on-chip cache using three coordinated mechanisms. Mat-Reorder rearranges one input matrix's columns to group frequently-accessed data together, enabling faster computation and early row completion. DP-Evict (Dead-Product Early Eviction) immediately frees cache space by removing fully-computed intermediate results, while RM-Caching (Reuse Distance-Aware Matrix Caching) prioritizes retaining matrix elements with short reuse distance (data needed again soon) in fast on-chip storage (SRAM) rather than slower main memory (DRAM). Together, these keep both matrices in a 6.15 mm² chip with minimal spillover to DRAM.
key_novelty: The core innovation is Mat-Reorder, which reorders columns of the sparse input matrix (a matrix with mostly zeros and few actual values) to align the processor's non-zero access patterns with what fits in the small on-chip cache, enabling both input matrices to stay cached simultaneously.
contributions: Mat-Reorder algorithm that reorders matrix columns to improve data locality and allow early row-computation completion
Dead-Product Early Eviction (DP-Evict) policy that reclaims on-chip memory as soon as partial products are finalized
Reuse Distance-Aware Matrix Caching (RM-Caching) that prioritizes high-reuse elements for on-chip retention
End-to-end SpMM accelerator (6.15 mm2) achieving 1.97x average speedup over state-of-the-art SpMM accelerators
baselines: state-of-the-art SpMM accelerator (unspecified, inferred from abstract)
limitations: The matrix reordering step incurs preprocessing overhead that may not be amortized for one-shot or highly dynamic sparse workloads.
primary_theme: on-chip cache optimization for sparse matrix multiplication
